prompt.adult: Eliphaz says man is born to trouble. In 5:7, what does he say fly upward?
prompt.child: One of Job’s friends says trouble comes to people as surely as something rises. What does he say flies upward?
prompt.teen: Job 5:7: “Yet man is born to trouble, As” what “fly upward”?
prompt.older: According to Job 5:7, what fly upward?

verses.text: Yet man is born to trouble, As the sparks fly upward.

explanation.child: Look at the end of Job 5:7.
explanation.teen: 5:7 has two lines: trouble, and then a picture. Read the picture.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:6 says affliction does not come from the dust. 5:8 goes on: “But as for me, I would seek God.”
teaching.takeaway: Man is born to trouble, “As the sparks fly upward.”

prompt.adult: Bildad speaks of all who forget God. In 8:14, what does he say their trust is?
prompt.child: Bildad says people who forget God trust in something weak. What does he compare it to?
prompt.older: According to Job 8:14, what is the trust of those who forget God?

verses.text: Whose confidence shall be cut off, And whose trust is a spider’s web.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 14.
explanation.teen: 8:14 has two lines: confidence cut off, then trust. Read the second.

teaching.extended_explanation: 8:13 says the hope of the hypocrite shall perish. 8:15 adds, “He leans on his house, but it does not stand.”

prompt.adult: Eliphaz asks Job, “Are you the first man who was born?” In 15:7, what does he ask whether Job was made before?
prompt.child: Job’s friend asks if Job was the very first man ever born. What else does he ask if Job was made before?
prompt.teen: Job 15:7: “Or were you made before” what?
prompt.older: According to Job 15:7, before what does Eliphaz ask whether Job was made?

verses.text: “Are you the first man who was born? Or were you made before the hills?
Have you heard the counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 7.
explanation.teen: 15:7 asks two questions. Read the end of the second.

teaching.extended_explanation: 15:8 goes on to ask whether Job has heard the counsel of God and whether he limits wisdom to himself.
teaching.takeaway: He asked, “Or were you made before the hills?”

prompt.adult: Elihu’s wrath was aroused against Job and against his three friends. According to 32:2, whose son was he?
prompt.child: A man named Elihu became angry and finally spoke up. Who was his father?
prompt.older: According to Job 32:2, who was Elihu’s father?

verses.text: Then the wrath of Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was aroused against Job; his wrath was aroused because he justified himself rather than God.
Also against his three friends his wrath was aroused, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

explanation.adult: Read the start of 32:2, after “Elihu, the son of.”
explanation.child: Look near the start of verse 2.
explanation.teen: 32:2 gives Elihu’s father and then his family. Read the father.

teaching.extended_explanation: 32:2 says Elihu was angry because Job justified himself rather than God. 32:3 says he was angry with the three friends because they had condemned Job.
teaching.takeaway: Elihu was the son of Barachel the Buzite.

prompt.adult: Elihu says he is full of words. In 32:19, he says he is ready to burst like what?
prompt.child: Elihu felt so full of things to say that he might burst. What did he say he was like?
prompt.teen: Job 32:19: “It is ready to burst like” what?
prompt.older: According to Job 32:19, what is Elihu ready to burst like?

verses.text: For I am full of words; The spirit within me compels me.
Indeed my belly is like wine that has no vent; It is ready to burst like new wineskins.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 19.
explanation.teen: 32:19 gives two pictures; the second closes the verse. Read it.
explanation.older: It follows “ready to burst like” in 32:19.

teaching.extended_explanation: 32:18 says the spirit within him compels him. 32:19 first gives a picture of something that has no vent.
teaching.takeaway: He was “ready to burst like new wineskins.”

prompt.adult: In 4:17 Eliphaz asks, “Can a man be more pure than his Maker?” In 33:6, what does Elihu say he also has been?
prompt.child: Elihu tells Job that he is just a man like him. How does he say he was made?
prompt.older: Linking Job 4:17 with 33:6, what does Elihu say he too has been?

verses.text: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Can a man be more pure than his Maker?
Truly I am as your spokesman before God; I also have been formed out of clay.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of Job 33:6.
explanation.teen: 4:17 is the setting; 33:6 has two lines. Read the end of the second.
explanation.older: It follows “I also have been” in 33:6.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:17 asks whether a mortal can be more righteous than God. 33:6 begins with Elihu saying he is as Job’s spokesman before God.
teaching.takeaway: He said, “I also have been formed out of clay.”

prompt.adult: Zophar asks in 11:7, “Can you search out the deep things of God?” In 36:26, what does Elihu say cannot be discovered?
prompt.child: Elihu says God is so great that we cannot fully know Him. What can no one discover?
prompt.older: Zophar and Elihu both speak of what cannot be known about God. According to 36:26, what cannot be discovered?

verses.text: “Can you search out the deep things of God? Can you find out the limits of the Almighty?
“Behold, God is great, and we do not know Him; Nor can the number of His years be discovered.

explanation.child: Look at the end of Job 36:26.
explanation.teen: 11:7 is the setting; 36:26 has two lines. Read the second.

teaching.extended_explanation: 11:8 says such things are higher than heaven and deeper than Sheol. 36:26 opens, “Behold, God is great, and we do not know Him.”
teaching.takeaway: Nor can “the number of His years be discovered.”

prompt.adult: Eliphaz in 5:17 calls the man whom God corrects happy. In 8:7, what does Bildad say Job’s latter end would do?
prompt.child: Bildad says that even though Job started small, his later days could change. What would they do?
prompt.teen: Job 8:7: “Yet your latter end would” do what?
prompt.older: Alongside Eliphaz’s word about correction in 5:17, what does Bildad say in 8:7 Job’s latter end would do?

verses.text: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects; Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
Though your beginning was small, Yet your latter end would increase abundantly.

explanation.child: Look at the end of Job 8:7.
explanation.teen: 5:17 is the setting; 8:7 sets the beginning beside the latter end. Read the second line.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:17 tells Job not to despise the chastening of the Almighty. 8:7 begins, “Though your beginning was small.”
